corpus_definition: A high, steep rock face by the sea or mountains.

forms.definition: a high, steep wall of rock, often next to the sea
forms.example: Be careful near the edge of the cliff.

syn.note: A very steep side of a high rock or mountain; a more formal, literary word.
A high, steep bank, often by a river or the sea; less common than cliff.
A rough, steep piece of rock, usually on a mountain.
Easy, general word: the hard stone a cliff is made of.

forms.note: There is no verb in this family.
There is no common adjective in this family.
There is no adverb in this family.

context.text: In the mountains near Chimgan there is a high cliff above the river. Birds build their nests on the cliff, so climbers must be careful.

reviewer_note: Two corpus rows with the same meaning merged (lowest CEFR B1). Compounds such as clifftop are left out.

corpus_definition: The land next to the large salt water areas.

forms.definition: the land next to the sea
forms.example: They live on the west coast.

syn.note: The land at the edge of the sea or a lake; coast is used for larger areas and for regions.
British English: a place by the sea where people go on holiday.
Easy word: the area of sand or stones by the sea, a small part of a coast.

forms.definition: to move forward without using power, like a bike going downhill
forms.example: We stopped pedalling and coasted down the hill.
forms.note: Belongs to coast = move without effort or power, not the land next to the sea.

forms.definition: on or near the land next to the sea
forms.example: Many coastal towns are busy in summer.

syn.note: Connected with the sea or ships; more formal.

ant.note: Inland places are far from the sea, like Tashkent.

forms.note: There is no adverb in this family.

context.text: Uzbekistan has no coast, so many families go to the sea in other countries. Last summer we stayed in a small coastal town and swam every day.

reviewer_note: Verb coast (move without power) is a different meaning, shown as other_meaning. Compounds coastline and coastguard are left out.

corpus_definition: a long box in which a dead person is buried

forms.definition: a long box that a dead body is put in before burial
forms.example: They carried the coffin slowly into the church.

syn.note: American English uses casket for the same box; in British English a casket is also a small box for jewels.
Easy, general word; a coffin is a special box for a dead person.

forms.note: There is no common verb in this family.
There is no adjective in this family.
There is no adverb in this family.

context.text: In the film, six men carried the coffin out of the old house. Everyone stood quietly as the coffin passed.

reviewer_note: Only one form exists; sensitive topic kept short and neutral.

corpus_definition: to suddenly fall down or fail completely

forms.definition: a sudden fall of a building or person, or a sudden failure
forms.example: The collapse of the bridge closed the road for a month.

syn.note: Easy, general word; a collapse is a sudden and complete fall.
Used when a business or plan stops working; collapse is more sudden.
When a system, machine or talks stop working.

forms.definition: to fall down suddenly, or to fail completely
forms.example: The old bridge collapsed under the weight of the truck.

syn.note: Easy word; collapse means a sudden fall, often of a whole building or person.
Used for roofs, walls and tunnels that fall inwards.
To break slowly into small pieces, like an old wall.
For a business or plan; collapse means it fails suddenly and completely.

forms.definition: able to be folded so that it takes less space
forms.example: We took a collapsible table to the picnic.
forms.note: Belongs to collapse = fold something to make it smaller, not falling down or failing.
There is no adverb in this family.

context.text: After three days of heavy rain, part of the old wall collapsed. Luckily, nobody was hurt in the collapse.

reviewer_note: Verb and noun are the same spelling (conversion). Collapsible belongs to the folding meaning, so it is other_meaning; no affix is claimed on it.

corpus_definition: someone that you work with at the same place

forms.definition: a person who works in the same place or company as you
forms.example: My colleague is helping me with this project.

syn.note: Same meaning; more common in American English.
Informal British English, often for people doing the same kind of job.
A person you work or do business with, often from another company.
Easy word, but a partner shares a business or a task with you, not just a workplace.

forms.note: There is no verb in this family.
There is no common adjective in this family.
There is no adverb in this family.

context.text: Malika has worked at the bank for five years. Her colleagues often ask her for help, and on Fridays the colleagues eat plov together.

reviewer_note: Headword is itself a person noun, so it stays the main noun entry; no other family forms.

corpus_definition: A group of things that you have gathered.

forms.definition: a group of things of one kind that someone has gathered
forms.example: He has a large stamp collection.

syn.note: A group of things that belong together, like a set of cups.
Easy, general word for several things or people together.
A mix of different kinds of things, not always gathered with care.

forms.definition: to bring things of one kind together, often as a hobby
forms.example: My grandfather collects old coins from Central Asia.

syn.note: To bring things together; collect suggests a hobby or careful choice.
Formal: to get more and more of something over time.
Easy word: to keep things so you can use or enjoy them later.

ant.note: To spread things in many different places instead of bringing them together.

forms.definition: worth gathering and keeping because people like to own it
forms.example: Old Soviet stamps are very collectable now.
forms.note: American spelling: collectible.

syn.note: Worth a lot of money; a collectable thing is wanted by people who keep such things.

forms.definition: shared or done by all the members of a group
forms.example: Cleaning the street was a collective effort.
forms.note: Belongs to collect = bring people together as a group, not gathering things as a hobby.

forms.definition: together, as a group
forms.example: The neighbours collectively decided to plant trees.
forms.note: Goes with collective = done by a whole group, not a hobby collection.

people.definition: a person who gathers things of one kind as a hobby
people.example: The stamp collector showed us his rarest stamps.

context.text: My brother collects old coins. His collection now has more than 300 coins, and some of them are very collectable.

reviewer_note: Headword is the -ion noun; collect is its base verb. Collective/collectively are the group meaning, so other_meaning. Collect in the sense 'pick someone up' is not shown.

corpus_definition: a person who tells jokes to make people laugh

forms.definition: a person whose job is to tell jokes and make people laugh
forms.example: The famous comedian made the audience laugh.

syn.note: A person who writes or tells funny stories; a more formal word.
Anyone whose job is to entertain people, for example a singer or a magician.
Easy word: a person who likes telling jokes, not usually as a job.
A performer in funny clothes and make-up, often in a circus.

forms.note: There is no verb in this family.

forms.definition: funny, or connected with funny films, plays and shows
forms.example: The film has some great comic moments.
forms.note: Comic is also a noun: a comic is a comedian, or a magazine with picture stories.

syn.note: Easy, everyday word with almost the same meaning.
A little more formal; often used for writing and stories.
Funny in a pleasant way; usually less strong than comic.

ant.note: Very sad, especially in plays and stories.

forms.definition: funny in a strange or silly way
forms.example: The puppy looked comical in its big hat.

syn.note: Easy, general word; comical often means funny without meaning to be.
So silly that people laugh at it; can be unkind.

forms.definition: in a funny or silly way
forms.example: The tiny car was comically small for such a tall man.

syn.note: In a funny way; a little more formal.
In a way that makes people smile or laugh.

ant.note: In a way that is not funny or joking.

people.definition: funny films, plays and shows, or the art of making people laugh
people.example: He loves watching comedy on TV after work.

people.definition: a woman who tells jokes and makes people laugh
people.example: The comedienne told stories about her mother-in-law.
people.note: Old-fashioned; today comedian is used for women and men.

context.text: Bobur is a comedian on a popular TV show in Tashkent. His comic stories about family weddings are so comical that my grandmother laughs until she cries.

reviewer_note: Headword is a person noun, so it stays the main noun entry; comedy goes in People & things as the field. Comic is not listed as a synonym because it is a family member.

corpus_definition: a group given authority to do a task, or a fee paid for work

forms.definition: money paid to someone for each thing they sell
forms.example: The agent earned a commission on every house sold.

syn.note: Money paid for a service; a commission is usually a percentage of a sale.
A part of every 100; a commission is often a percentage of the price.
Easy, general word for money that is paid.

forms.definition: to officially ask an artist or writer to make something for you
forms.example: The city commissioned a new statue for the park.
forms.note: Belongs to commission = an order for a piece of work, not money for selling.

forms.definition: to do something wrong or against the law
forms.example: The police believe he committed the robbery.
forms.note: Belongs to commission = the act of doing a crime (formal: 'the commission of a crime'), not money for selling.
There is no common adjective in this meaning.
There is no adverb in this family.

people.definition: a member of an official group, or the head of a government department
people.example: The police commissioner spoke to the reporters.
people.note: Belongs to commission = an official group, not money for selling.

context.text: Dilshod sells cars in Samarkand. He gets a commission of two percent on each car, and last month his commission was bigger than his salary.

reviewer_note: CORPUS: the one row's definition joins two meanings (official group / fee); its example is the fee meaning. Split into Money and Group maps on the same word_id.

corpus_definition: a group given authority to do a task, or a fee paid for work

forms.definition: an official group of people chosen to check or decide something
forms.example: The government set up a commission to study air pollution.

syn.note: A group chosen to make decisions; a commission is usually more official and often set up by a government.
A group that controls a company or organization.
A small group of experts who give advice or judge something.
Easy, general word for people together.

forms.definition: to officially ask an artist or writer to make something for you
forms.example: The museum commissioned a painting of the old city.
forms.note: Belongs to commission = an order for a piece of work, not an official group.

forms.definition: to do something wrong or against the law
forms.example: The police believe he committed the robbery.
forms.note: Belongs to commission = the act of doing a crime (formal: 'the commission of a crime'), not an official group.
There is no common adjective in this meaning.
There is no adverb in this family.

people.definition: a member of an official group with special power
people.example: Each commissioner will visit five schools this month.

context.text: The election commission met in Tashkent on Monday. One commissioner said the new rules will be ready next month.

reviewer_note: CORPUS: the one row's definition joins two meanings (official group / fee). This is the Group map; the fee meaning has its own Money map.

corpus_definition: the group of people who live in the same area.

forms.definition: all the people who live in one area, town or neighbourhood
forms.example: Everyone in the community helped clean the park.

syn.note: An area of a town and the people in it; American spelling: neighborhood.
A much bigger group: all the people in a country.
The number of people living in a place, not the group itself.
Easy, general word for men, women and children.

forms.note: There is no verb made from this word.
There is no adjective made from this word. Communal shares an old root with community but is not made from it.
There is no adverb in this family.

context.text: In our mahalla, the whole community helps when a family has a wedding. People from the community cook plov and set up the tables together.

reviewer_note: Two corpus rows with the same meaning merged (B1). Communal shares an old root but is not made from community, so it is listed as not_family.

corpus_definition: small and neatly arranged to save space

forms.definition: the quality of being small and using little space
forms.example: People like this phone for its compactness.

syn.note: Being small; compactness also means everything is neatly fitted in.

forms.definition: a small flat case with a mirror and face powder
forms.example: She took a compact out of her bag and checked her face.
forms.note: Belongs to compact = a small make-up case, not the quality of being small.

forms.definition: to press something together so that it becomes hard and tight
forms.example: The heavy trucks compacted the soil on the road.
forms.note: Belongs to compact = pressed tightly together, not small and neatly arranged.

forms.definition: small and arranged neatly so that it saves space
forms.example: She bought a compact camera for the trip.

syn.note: Easy word; compact means small in a useful, well-planned way.
Tidy and well arranged.
Easy to carry; compact things are often portable.

ant.note: Big and taking up a lot of space, so hard to carry or store.

forms.definition: in a small, neat way that saves space
forms.example: Everything in the tiny kitchen is arranged compactly.

syn.note: In a tidy, careful way; compactly also means using little space.
Closely together, with no space between.

context.text: My new flat in Chilonzor is very compact. The kitchen is arranged so compactly that I can reach everything from one place.

reviewer_note: Noun compact (make-up case) and verb compact (press together) are other meanings. Compound compact disc is left out.
